title: Rachmaninoff and Richter: the Moderato opening
work: Piano Concerto No. 2, Op. 18 — I. Moderato, opening-side comparison only
question: How do the composer and Richter pace the opening when the piano moves between chords, accompaniment and melody?
intro: Rachmaninoff recorded the concerto with Stokowski and the Philadelphia Orchestra on 10 April 1929; the reference is Richter with Wisłocki and the Warsaw National Philharmonic Orchestra in 1959. This comparison uses only HMV D.B. 1333’s first side, matching Richter’s opening 0–207 seconds to 3–179 seconds of the historical transfer, not reconstructing the complete movement. The provisional map has median chroma confidence 0.934 after a one-semitone adjustment to the historical pitch-class features alone. Playback remains untouched, so the timing describes these supplied transfers rather than speed-corrected historical performances; the Archive also reports wow and minor distortion.

maps.pitchEvidence: cache/analysis/rachmaninoff-concerto-2-moderato-rachmaninoff-1929-side1.txt repeatedly estimates C-sharp-minor pitch content where the reference report estimates C minor. tools/compare.py --transpose-b 1 rolls historical chroma down one semitone, not the audio. This does not establish original tuning or a uniform transfer-speed error.
maps.inspection: Ten-second path samples advance through [30,29.19], [100,83.96] and [150,127.46]. Early noisy windows and the map edges are not used for precise tempo claims. Confidence is pitch-class similarity, not proof of beat-exact correspondence.
